stanzas.sanskrit:
कुचेलनामा भवतः सतीर्थ्यतां
गतः स सान्दीपनिमन्दिरे द्विजः ।
त्वदेकरागेण धनादिनिःस्पृहो
दिनानि निन्ये प्रशमी गृहाश्रमी ॥ ८७-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The Brahmin by the name Kuchela (Sudaamaa) studied in the Sandipani ashram along with Krishna. He was totally devoted to Krishna & had a controlled mind. He lived without any worldly desires.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kucelanāmā bhavataḥ satīrthyatāṃ
gataḥ sa sāndīpanimandire dvijaḥ |
tvadekarāgeṇa dhanādiniḥspṛho
dināni ninye praśamī gṛhāśramī || 87-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
समानशीलाऽपि तदीयवल्लभा
तथैव नो चित्तजयं समेयुषी ।
कदाचिदूचे बत वृत्तिलब्धये
रमापतिः किं न सखा निषेव्यते ॥ ८७-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kuchela's wife was equally of the same nature, but with less balanced state of mind. One day, she suggested to go and meet his friend Krishna to get some means for their livelihood.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
samānaśīlā’pi tadīyavallabhā
tathaiva no cittajayaṃ sameyuṣī |
kadācidūce bata vṛttilabdhaye
ramāpatiḥ kiṃ na sakhā niṣevyate || 87-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
इतीरितोऽयं प्रियया क्षुधार्तया
जुगुप्समानोऽपि धने मदावहे ।
तदा त्वदालोकनकौतुकाद्ययौ
वहन् पटान्ते पृथुकानुपायनम् ॥ ८७-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kuchels's wife suggested so only because of their hunger miseries. Kuchela did not have interest in wealth and knows that possession of it, can make one mad. In his eagerness to meet Krishna, he left with some beaten rice folded and kept in his cloth, to offer to Krishna.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
itīrito’yaṃ priyayā kṣudhārtayā
jugupsamāno’pi dhane madāvahe |
tadā tvadālokanakautukādyayau
vahan paṭānte pṛthukānupāyanam || 87-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
गतोऽयमाश्चर्यमयीं भवत्पूरीं
गृहेषु शैब्याभवनं समेयिवान् ।
प्रविश्य वैकुण्ठमिवाप निर्वृतिं
तवातिसम्भावनया तु किं पुनः ॥ ८७-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: When Kuchela entered Dwaraka, he felt happy as though he has entered Vaikuntam. Krishna welcomed him with honours which made Kuchela more happy.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
gato’yamāścaryamayīṃ bhavatpūrīṃ
gṛheṣu śaibyābhavanaṃ sameyivān |
praviśya vaikuṇṭhamivāpa nirvṛtiṃ
tavātisambhāvanayā tu kiṃ punaḥ || 87-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रपूजितं तं प्रियया च वीजितं
करे गृहीत्वाऽकथयः पुराकृतम् ।
यदिन्धनार्थं गुरुदारचोदितै-
-रपर्तुवर्षं तदमर्षि कानने ॥ ८७-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna asked HIS wife to fan for Kuchela and HE did the pooja. Krishna held the hands of Kuchela and recollected old memories. Like when Guru pathni sent them to forest to gather fire wood and were caught in rain in the forest.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
prapūjitaṃ taṃ priyayā ca vījitaṃ
kare gṛhītvā’kathayaḥ purākṛtam |
yadindhanārthaṃ gurudāracoditai-
-rapartuvarṣaṃ tadamarṣi kānane || 87-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्रपाजुषोऽस्मात् पृथुकं बलादथ
प्रगृह्य मुष्टौ सकृदाशिते त्वया ।
कृतं कृतं नन्वियतेति सम्भ्रमा-
-द्रमा किलोपेत्य करं रुरोध ते ॥ ८७-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kuchela was feeling very shy and Krishna forcefully snatched the flattened rice from him and ate a fistful. Just then Rukmini approached Krishna and held back Krishna’s hand saying that it was enough.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
trapājuṣo’smāt pṛthukaṃ balādatha
pragṛhya muṣṭau sakṛdāśite tvayā |
kṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ nanviyateti sambhramā-
-dramā kilopetya karaṃ rurodha te || 87-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भक्तेषु भक्तेन स मानितस्त्वया
पुरीं वसन्नेकनिशां महासुखम् ।
बतापरेद्युर्द्रविणं विना ययौ
विचित्ररूपस्तव खल्वनुग्रहः ॥ ८७-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kuchela was greatly honoured by Krishna. the devoted of the devotees, and very happily stayed in Thy city for one night. The next day he went away alas without any wealth. Strange indeed are Bhagwan’s forms of blessings.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhakteṣu bhaktena sa mānitastvayā
purīṃ vasannekaniśāṃ mahāsukham |
batāparedyurdraviṇaṃ vinā yayau
vicitrarūpastava khalvanugrahaḥ || 87-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
यदि ह्ययाचिष्यमदास्यदच्युतो
वदामि भार्यां किमिति व्रजन्नसौ ।
त्वदुक्तिलीलास्मितमग्नधीः पुनः
क्रमादपश्यन् मणिदीप्रमालयम् ॥ ८७-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kuchela wondered what answer he can give to his wife. Actually if he had requested wealth, Krishna would have surely given. But he drowned himself in the thoughts of happy times spent with Krishna and reached a gem studded splendorous mansion.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
yadi hyayāciṣyamadāsyadacyuto
vadāmi bhāryāṃ kimiti vrajannasau |
tvaduktilīlāsmitamagnadhīḥ punaḥ
kramādapaśyan maṇidīpramālayam || 87-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
किं मार्गविभ्रंश इति भ्रमन् क्षणं
गृहं प्रविष्टः स ददर्श वल्लभाम् ।
सखीपरीतां मणिहेमभूषितां
बुबोध च त्वत्करुणां महाद्भुताम् ॥ ८७-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kuchela wondered if he lost his way & with doubt entered the house. He saw his wife adorned in ornaments of gems and gold and surrounded by her friends. He realised it was Bhagwan’s grace and compassion.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kiṃ mārgavibhraṃśa iti bhraman kṣaṇaṃ
gṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ sa dadarśa vallabhām |
sakhīparītāṃ maṇihemabhūṣitāṃ
bubodha ca tvatkaruṇāṃ mahādbhutām || 87-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
स रत्नशालासु वसन्नपि स्वयं
समुन्नमद्भक्तिभरोऽमृतं ययौ ।
त्वमेवमापूरितभक्तवाञ्छितो
मरुत्पुराधीश हरस्व मे गदान् ॥ ८७-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Though Kuchela lived in the ornamental mansion, he spent his days fixing his mind on Krishna and after living long time, he reached Moksham.
Bhattathiri worshipped Bhagwan to cure his ailments.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sa ratnaśālāsu vasannapi svayaṃ
samunnamadbhaktibharo’mṛtaṃ yayau |
tvamevamāpūritabhaktavāñchito
marutpurādhīśa harasva me gadān || 87-10 ||
